questions.question: Which invariant best prevents a streamed request from becoming unaccountable after a retry or fallback?
options: Each worker creates a new request ID
Admission, scheduling, execution, safety, and streaming share one request ID and deadline
Only the API gateway records timing
The model chooses its own timeout
questions.explanation: A single request contract lets every component attribute work, enforce the same remaining budget, and propagate cancellation consistently.

questions.question: Why can a request fit model weights in accelerator memory but still be rejected by the scheduler?
options: KV cache for its context and output reserve may exceed the allocated cache budget
Prefill never uses memory
Decode removes the need for cache
Queue delay is always zero for loaded models
questions.explanation: Weights are only part of serving memory. Active sequences reserve KV cache that grows with context, output, concurrency, and model architecture.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of continuous batching for uneven generations?
options: It guarantees no queueing
It lets sequences enter and leave between decode steps so short work need not wait for every long sequence
It removes the need for memory admission
It makes every model response identical
questions.explanation: Continuous batching can improve packing across variable output lengths, but it still needs cache-aware admission and fairness controls.

questions.question: A safety dependency times out for a high-risk tool action. What is the defensible default?
options: Bypass safety to preserve availability
Retry forever until the deadline is exceeded
Fail closed or defer because the action cannot preserve its safety contract
Stream the action and validate it later
questions.explanation: High-risk actions need their safety boundary. A dependency timeout does not authorize an unvalidated action.

questions.question: Which autoscaling signal is most useful for protecting interactive users before workers are fully saturated?
options: Queue wait and time to first token, together with active sequences and cache allocation
Only total deployed workers
Only average output length from yesterday
Only accelerator temperature
questions.explanation: Queue wait and TTFT capture pending user pain, while active sequences and cache allocation explain whether more work can actually be admitted.

questions.question: When a client disconnects from a live token stream, what should normally happen?
options: Continue generating indefinitely
Cancel the request through scheduler and worker and release its cache
Reuse the output for the next tenant
Remove the request ID from telemetry
questions.explanation: Unless the product explicitly created a durable job with separate storage and deadline, disconnected streaming work should be canceled to free capacity.
